summaryPoints: West Indies built a commanding first-innings platform of 354, spearheaded by KC Brathwaite's brilliant 126.

A resilient final-day rearguard ensured the match concluded in a fiercely contested draw.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Sir Vivian Richards Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as West Indies posted 354/10 (111.1 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Sri Lanka countered with 258/10 (106.6 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Century: KC Brathwaite 126 (311b), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, KC Brathwaite delivered a masterclass for West Indies (211 Runs), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Match Drawn 47%) and allowing Match Drawn to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Sri Lanka faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Match Drawn's bowling unit, bolstered by KR Mayers (104 Runs & 2 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Match drawn in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Match Drawn's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Sri Lanka produced fighting phases, Match Drawn won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
